mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where GDPC1 shows a sustained 3-month increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals weakening labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE rises by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) declines by more than 1% in a month, it signals supply chain disruptions and reduced economic output, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO declines by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real GDP (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where GDPC1 and RSAFS both show increases.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure during a tightening cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS is above 5% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a month signals weakening labor market conditions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where PAYEMS decreases by more than 100,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) indicates weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST shows a sustained 3-month decline.
